newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was inactive on Tuesday as owners anticipated steady to higher prices this week, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids at $62.00 to $63.00 were countered by owners asking mostly $65.00, with a few at $66.00.
Packers reportedly were well supplied with live cattle inventories following last week's active sales and would likely wait another day before buying more, several cattle feeders said.
When trades do emerge, they were expected at steady to $1.00 higher prices, compared with a week ago, they said.
Fed cattle prices last week were at $64.00, up $2.00 from the previous week.

Packers reportedly were slow returning to the market because of sluggish beef movement so far this week, the feedlot sources said. Advances since July 10 reportedly have chased away some potential retail buyers, they said.
Boxed beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.26 to $0.48 per cwt for choice cuts and down $0.33 to $0.39 for selects, with 179 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
Beef movement by midday Tuesday at 229 loads was below the total of 298 sold Monday and Tuesday last week.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $102.90, up $0.26 from Monday and up $3.86 since prices started climbing after July 10, USDA statistics showed.
